dedupe_keys.name: parametric fragility curves for atmospheric storage tanks and tank groups natech approach

description: This model derives fragility curves for large cylindrical storage tanks from a parametric model of each tank, not from historical damage records, so that curves can be produced for many tank configurations and storage park layouts. It also gives a formulation for groups of tanks exposed to the same extreme event, and illustrates both with examples, aiming at technological accidents triggered by natural hazards (Natech), such as releases of hazardous materials after earthquakes, tsunamis or storms. It was developed by Santiago Zuluaga Mayorga, Mauricio Sánchez-Silva, Oscar J. Ramírez Olivar and Felipe Muñoz Giraldo and published in Reliability Engineering and System Safety, volume 189, in September 2019; the affiliation is not given in the pages read. It is generic in location. The article is behind Elsevier's subscription access, and the pages read do not mention code. Caveats: it covers only ground-supported tanks storing liquid at atmospheric pressure, not elevated, rectangular or pressurised tanks, and the publisher's page could not be read from the cloud, so this record rests on the RePEc abstract and Crossref metadata. For simulation it provides damage probabilities for tank farms at refineries, chemical plants and ports, feeding Natech risk, hazardous release and cascading failure models. It is related to the Natech H2S release case study record in this catalogue.
